Subject: Queue prioritization for deal-dependent onramp (Acme AI)

Hi Marta / Cloud team,

Quick context: Acme AI (deal ACME-2029-DED-03) is finalizing a Dedicated onramp that starts in Q2. Their contract asks for an initial capacity window that maps to two hardware tranches (aggressive: 40 A100-class equivalents in month 1, follow-on 80 in month 3). We need explicit OEM and cloud signals to craft a clean mutual action plan and avoid a delivery gap.

Attached: slot_prioritization_matrix.xlsx (proposed allocation by tranche + week windows).

Asks:
- Marta: can you confirm estimated ship windows for a two-tranche split (partial ship + remainder) and a firm ETA range per tranche, with lead-times and any expedite options (pricing + required deposit)? Please attach an updated OEM quote with line items for expedite and staging.
- Cloud Sales: can you confirm reserved instance / host availability in us-west-2 as a formal backfill option, and provide a short lead-time to reserve capacity (and cost delta vs on-demand)?
- Internal: Ben/Laura/Vanessa — I need a draft mutual action plan by EOD Thu so we can attach to the SOW.

We will escalate to procurement if we see conflicting windows. Hoping to converge quickly so Acme can close their internal procurement and we can schedule onboarding.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic GTM
Redwood Inference

From: Marta Ruiz <marta.ruiz@oemco.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: supply@oemco.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jan 2029 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Queue prioritization for deal-dependent onramp (Acme AI)

Karthik —

Thanks for the clear matrix. High level OEM signal below (attached as OEM_quote_ACME_v4.pdf). Note these are production windows based on current manufacturing cadence and downstream allocation rules:

- Tranche A (partial): 12–14 weeks from PO + deposit. We can commit to shipping 40 units in a single outbound if deposit hits within 5 business days of PO acceptance.
- Tranche B (remainder): 18–22 weeks from PO for remaining 80 units (slot contingent on current queue; we can hedge by assigning a tranche number in our allocation system).

Options / caveats:
- Expedite lane: +12% on hardware list price, reduces first-tranche ETA to 8–10 weeks but limited to two expedite slots per quarter. Requires 50% non-refundable deposit and signed expedited addendum.
- Staging shipment: we can split Tranche A into two smaller shipments (20/20) to hit an earlier partial delivery (first 20 in 8–9 weeks, next 20 in 12 weeks) — increases logistic complexity and per-shipment customs exposure.
- Customs / ports: if you need guaranteed month-level arrival windows, add 2–3 weeks buffer for cross-border routes — we recommend using our logistics partner for consolidated clearance.

I've attached the quote and line items (OEM_quote_ACME_v4.pdf). Please note our allocation number will be held for 14 days after PO receipt. If Redwood requires a longer hold, we can discuss a paid hold fee.

Let me know if you want us to provision a binding slot hold; if so, share the PO and the deposit authorization contact.

Regards,
Marta Ruiz
Head of Strategic Accounts, OEMCo

Hi Karthik / team,

We can offer a US-West-2 reserved host pool intended for dedicated onramps. Summary:
- Reserved host pool lead: 4–6 weeks to standby (service activation + control-plane prep) if contracted this week.
- Capacity: up to ~120 A100-equivalents across a single AZ with burst capability to other AZs for short periods.
- Cost: ~20% premium vs on-demand for reserved hosts (volume pricing applies).
- SLA: 99.9% regional uptime; cross-AZ failover is not guaranteed for sustained loads (we recommend a staged cutover).

We can add a short-term credit to offset the first-month premium if you commit to a 6-month reserved term. Attached: cloud_capacity_offer.docx.

If OEM lead times push beyond 12 weeks for the first tranche, we recommend using our reserved host pool for an initial ramp and then shifting workloads to OEM hardware as it arrives. We'll need an anticipated activation date and a signature authority to hold the pool.

Regards,
Cloud Sales Team
BigCloud Corp.

All — quick internal summary and recommended MAP for commercial approval:

Summary of external signals:
- OEM: Tranche A possible 12–14 weeks (8–10 weeks with expedite + 50% deposit).
- Cloud: Reserved pool available in 4–6 weeks if we contract now.

Recommended mutual action plan (draft):
1) Redwood to send PO for Tranche A with 30% deposit to lock allocation (we keep negotiation to expedite fee optional).
2) OEM to hold allocation for 14 days on PO receipt; if we need >14 days, opt for paid hold (TBD).
3) Redwood to sign 3-month reserved host term with BigCloud, with a credit applied to month 1. Activate reserve in week 6.
4) Run initial onboarding on BigCloud reserved hosts for weeks 6–12, then migrate to OEM hardware as first shipments arrive.
5) Finance to confirm deposit approval and payment run; legal to review expedited addendum if chosen.

Immediate asks:
- Laura: confirm legal can turn the expedited addendum in 48 hours if we choose expedite.
- Vanessa: confirm procurement can authorize 30% deposit within 3 business days to meet OEM 14-day hold.

If we land the deposit and reserve, we can guarantee the customer an effective start in 6–8 weeks while preserving the full hardware-on-prem commitment.

—Ben
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
